Positive Neumann heat diffusion supplies strictly positive infected mass on every distant finite interval at t0>0. Pick a Dirichlet test slab [L*,L*+H] with growth exponent eta=k a L*−mu−D pi²/(2H²)>0, compare against c exp(eta(t−t0)) sin(pi(λ−L*)/H), forcing I(t)→∞ contrary to population ≤1. On bounded traits, integrate log(S0/S∞)≤(kL/mu)(S0+I0−S∞), whose strictly convex root geometry gives S∞≥u_L>0, sharp as diffusion→0 with initial infected density concentrating at L. At D=0 compact support bounds traits, S∞>0; finite-horizon semigroup continuity yields noncommuting limits. Independent sample with k=2,mu=1,D=1,a=0.1,L*=40,H=1 gave eta≈2.065>0, illustrative only.
